topic.name: [Course] - Microsoft Power BI para Business Intelligence e Data Science

questions.question_text:
Complete the DAX measure that returns the total sales:

```dax
Total Sales = ____(Fact_Sales[Sales])
```
questions.explanation: SUM adds the values of a column in the current filter context. The other functions compute an average, a row count, or a count of distinct values.

questions.question_text:
Complete the Power Query step that replaces every "?" with null, only in the named column:

```m
NoQuestionMarks = Table.ReplaceValue(Promoted, "?", null, Replacer.ReplaceValue, {"____"})
```
questions.explanation: The list argument limits the replacement to the named columns. Replacing "?" before the type conversion matters, because a text column accepts "?" as a valid value.

questions.question_text: Profit is defined per order line as $\text{Profit}_i = \text{Sales}_i - \text{Shipping}_i$. Which expression gives the profit margin percentage over all lines?
questions.explanation: The margin is the ratio of summed profit to summed sales, so every dollar of sales counts equally. An average of line margins would give a small line the same weight as a large one.

questions.question_text: Average ticket is $\frac{\sum_i \text{Sales}_i}{|\{\text{Order ID}\}|}$. What does the denominator count?
questions.explanation: The denominator counts distinct order IDs. An order with two lines is counted once, so the average is per order, not per line.

questions.question_text: Which Power Platform product is used to build chatbots?
questions.explanation: Power Virtual Agents builds chatbots. Power Automate automates workflows, Power Apps builds custom apps, and Power BI analyzes and visualizes data.

questions.question_text: Which Power BI version embeds dashboards inside a web application?
questions.explanation: Power BI Embedded places dashboards inside web applications, so users see them within the application itself.

questions.question_text: In a star schema, what does a fact table store?

options.A: Numeric measures recorded at the grain of one event, linked to dimension tables by keys
options.D: Descriptive attributes such as names and regions

questions.explanation: The fact table holds measures at a defined grain, such as one order line. Dimension tables describe the entities those rows refer to.

questions.question_text: Which visual shows the share of a whole across many categories as proportional areas?
questions.explanation: A treemap sizes each rectangle by its share of the total, which suits more categories than a waterfall chart.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of a slicer in a Power BI report?

options.A: Publishing the report to mobile devices
options.B: Filtering the visuals on the page interactively

questions.explanation: A slicer lets viewers filter all linked visuals on the page without editing the model.

questions.question_text: What does the Column Distribution view in Power Query show?

options.A: The DAX formulas of the model
options.C: Small distribution charts, outliers and distinct values for each column

questions.explanation: Column Distribution shows the spread of values, outliers and the number of distinct and unique values, which helps spot data quality issues early.

questions.question_text:
Complete the 3-month moving average measure. The date table is marked as a date table.

```dax
Sales MA3 =
CALCULATE(
    AVERAGE(Fact_Sales[sales]),
    ____(Dim_Month[month], MAX(Dim_Month[month]), -3, MONTH)
)
```
questions.explanation: DATESINPERIOD returns a window of dates that ends at the latest selected month and goes back three months, so the average covers exactly those months.

questions.question_text:
Complete the measure so it returns a blank instead of a division error when total sales is zero:

```dax
Profit Margin % = ____([Didactic Profit], [Total Sales])
```
questions.explanation: DIVIDE is the safe division function in DAX. It returns a blank, or an alternate result you pass, when the denominator is zero.

questions.question_text: A monthly target for average sale value is 350. Which expression gives the target attainment percentage for a month whose average sale value is $\bar{x}_m$?
questions.explanation: Attainment is the actual value divided by the target, times 100. An average of 280 against 350 gives 80%.

questions.question_text: Which formula gives the year-over-year growth of monthly sales $S_m$?
questions.explanation: Growth compares the month with the same month one year earlier, which is 12 steps back in monthly data. Dividing by the earlier value turns the difference into a percentage.

questions.question_text: Why should a date table be marked as a date table before using time intelligence functions?

options.A: So the columns are hidden from the report
options.C: So the report can be published to mobile
options.D: So the time functions can rely on a continuous, unique date column

questions.explanation: Time intelligence functions need one row per date with no gaps. Marking the table tells Power BI which column to use.

questions.question_text: Why is DISTINCTCOUNT preferred over COUNT when counting orders that have several lines?

options.A: It counts each order ID once, however many lines it has
options.B: It is faster on every dataset
options.C: It ignores blank values in the sales column

questions.explanation: COUNT would count order lines. DISTINCTCOUNT of the order ID counts each order once, which is the right unit for order-level metrics.

questions.question_text: In Power Query, which action keeps only the first row for each CustomerID?

options.B: Remove duplicates on the CustomerID column
options.D: Filter rows where Age is null

questions.explanation: Removing duplicates by a key keeps one row per key value, which prevents a customer from being counted several times.

questions.question_text: A dashboard must compare actual sales with a target using a single headline number. Which visual fits best?
questions.explanation: A KPI visual shows one actual value against its goal and the status, which is the purpose of a headline indicator.

questions.question_text: Which layout practice most improves the legibility of a Power BI dashboard?

options.A: Maximum number of colors for every series
options.B: No titles, so the charts speak for themselves
options.D: Few visuals per page, clear titles and a consistent color style

questions.explanation: Clear titles, few visuals and a consistent palette let readers find the message quickly. Dense, multicolor pages slow interpretation.

questions.question_text:
Complete the Power Query step that keeps one row per customer:

```m
NoDuplicates = Table.____(Promoted, {"CustomerID"})
```
questions.explanation: Table.Distinct keeps the first row for each key combination, which is how duplicate customer rows are removed.

questions.question_text:
This measure averages the sales of each selected ship mode, so a selection of several modes returns the wrong total. Complete the correct version:

```dax
Sales Per Mode = ____(VALUES(Dim_ShipMode[ShipMode]), [Total Sales])
```
questions.explanation: SUMX adds the measure across the selected modes, so the result equals the total for the selection. AVERAGEX would divide that total by the number of modes.

questions.question_text:
Complete the step that reads order dates written in the Brazilian Portuguese format:

```m
Dates = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, {{"OrderDate", type date}}, "____")
```
questions.explanation: The culture argument controls how text dates are parsed. Without it, 03/04 can be read as March 4 or April 3 depending on the machine.

questions.question_text:
A forecast model is fitted on 36 months and tested on the last 6. Which accuracy measure should choose the model?

$$
\text{MAPE} = \frac{100}{h}\sum_{t \in \text{holdout}} \left|\frac{y_t - \hat{y}_t}{y_t}\right|
$$

options.A: MAPE computed on the holdout months, where $h$ is the number of held-out months
options.C: The ratio of the mean forecast to the mean actual
options.D: MAPE computed on the training fit only

questions.explanation: The model must be judged on months it did not see during fitting. Error on the holdout shows out-of-sample accuracy, while training fit can look good because the model adapted to those months.

questions.question_text: Under the interquartile rule, with $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$, which condition flags a value $x$ as an outlier?
questions.explanation: The IQR fences are two-sided and depend on the spread of the middle half of the data, so they are robust to extreme values. The 3-sigma rule uses the mean and standard deviation, which extreme values distort.

questions.question_text: A monthly sales series shows a repeating yearly pattern and a steady upward drift. Which model captures both components explicitly?

options.B: Holt-Winters with additive trend and additive seasonality
options.C: A simple moving average of one month

questions.explanation: Holt-Winters models level, trend and seasonality explicitly. A moving average of one month removes neither the seasonality nor the drift.

questions.question_text: Before choosing the number of customer segments with clustering, which two checks justify the choice?

options.A: The number of rows in the dashboard
options.B: The date of the last refresh
options.C: The elbow in inertia and the silhouette score across candidate values of k
options.D: The number of colors in the report theme

questions.explanation: Inertia shows where adding clusters stops reducing error much, and the silhouette score shows how well separated the clusters are. Together they justify k.

questions.question_text: Why apply a log transform before standardizing recency, frequency and monetary features for segmentation?

options.D: Heavily skewed spending would otherwise dominate the distance between customers

questions.explanation: A skewed feature with very large values dominates Euclidean distance. The log transform reduces the skew, and standardization then puts the features on the same scale.

questions.question_text: A dashboard computes a KPI for each segment and then averages the segment KPIs. Why can the result differ from the KPI computed over all rows?

options.A: The average of ratios ignores segment sizes, while the ratio of summed parts weights each row equally
options.B: The dashboard rounds each segment separately

questions.explanation: An unweighted average of segment ratios treats a small segment like a large one. The correct approach is to aggregate the sums first and then divide.

questions.question_text: When several teams calculate the same KPI in their own reports, what failure appears first?

options.A: Higher license cost of Power BI Desktop
options.B: Different numbers for the same metric, which damages trust in every report
options.C: Slower refresh of the source database

questions.explanation: Competing definitions produce conflicting numbers, and the loss of trust is the primary damage. Governed shared measures prevent it.

questions.question_text: What is the main reason to keep simple rule-based baselines, such as a z-score or IQR rule, when evaluating an anomaly detection model?

options.A: They replace the need for labeled data
options.C: They define the minimum performance any learned model must beat on labeled cases
options.D: They are required by the report theme

questions.explanation: A baseline is the bar a more complex model must clear. If a learned model does not beat simple rules on labeled cases, its extra complexity is not justified.

questions.question_text:
A CEO wants one definition of profit margin that every report reuses. Complete the shared measure:

```dax
Profit Margin % = DIVIDE(____, [Total Sales])
```
questions.explanation: One governed measure defines the ratio in one place. Every report that reuses it inherits the same numerator and denominator, so the margin cannot drift between teams.

questions.question_text:
A shared cleaning function must return a number from text, and it is reused across datasets. Complete the final step:

```m
(value as nullable text) as nullable number =>
    let
        cleaned = Text.Replace(value, "?", "")
    in
        ____(cleaned)
```
questions.explanation: A reusable function turns the cleaned text into a number, so every dataset that calls it gets the same parsing rule. This is how a cleaning standard scales beyond one report.

questions.question_text:
A CEO compares business units of very different sizes. Which metric gives a fair comparison of profitability?

$$
\frac{\sum_{u} \text{Profit}_u}{\sum_{u} \text{Sales}_u}
$$

options.A: The unit with the highest single profit line
options.B: The ratio of summed profit to summed sales across units
options.C: The mean of each unit's profit divided by its sales

questions.explanation: The ratio of sums weights each unit by its sales, so large and small units are compared on the same basis. A mean of ratios treats a small unit like a large one.

questions.question_text:
A roadmap must choose a forecasting model. Forecast error on the holdout is $e_t = y_t - \hat{y}_t$. Which decision rule best supports the investment?

$$
\text{choose the model minimizing } \frac{1}{h}\sum_{t=1}^{h} |e_t|
$$

options.A: The model with the highest training R-squared
options.C: The model with the smallest error on the training data
options.D: The model with the smallest mean absolute error over the h held-out months

questions.explanation: Held-out error approximates how the model will behave on future months. Training error rewards overfitting, and complexity alone does not improve forecasts.

questions.question_text: The company plans to reuse one semantic model across all departments to cut reporting costs. Which is the main risk to manage?

options.A: Power BI cannot share a model across reports
options.B: Each department must buy its own license for the model
options.C: The model stops refreshing after one month
options.D: A change to a shared definition propagates to every report, so versioning and governance must control it

questions.explanation: Reuse multiplies both the benefit and the blast radius of a change. Governance, ownership and versioning of shared definitions protect the investment.

questions.question_text: Why does a scaled BI program invest in data lineage and governance?

options.A: So any number can be traced to its sources and transformations for audit and trust
options.B: So dashboards load faster on mobile
options.C: So the date table can be removed

questions.explanation: Lineage shows where a figure came from. Auditable traceability is what lets executives trust a number that drives a decision.

questions.question_text: Before adding fraud-oriented anomaly detection to the roadmap, which question should the CEO ask first?

options.B: What is the cost of false alarms compared with the cost of missed cases?
options.C: Which chart colors match the brand?
options.D: How many visuals fit on a page?

questions.explanation: The decision threshold depends on the relative cost of false positives and false negatives. That trade-off sets the acceptable model behavior before any technical choice.

questions.question_text: A company centralizes one model for all departments. Which trade-off does it accept?

options.A: No trade-off, because the model is shared
options.B: Lower security in exchange for speed
options.C: Consistent definitions across departments in exchange for slower local changes
options.D: Faster local changes in exchange for inconsistent numbers

questions.explanation: Centralization buys one set of definitions, which is valuable, but local teams must go through the shared model to change a metric.

questions.question_text: Which strategic indicator best shows that Power BI is changing decisions, not only producing reports?

options.A: The number of pages published per month
options.B: The number of visuals per dashboard
options.C: The number of users who opened the report once
options.D: Decisions taken at KPI reviews that are traceably linked to a specific metric and its target

questions.explanation: Impact shows up when a recorded decision cites a metric and its target. Page counts and one-time views measure activity, not influence.

questions.question_text: Why does a sound BI roadmap put descriptive analytics before predictive models?

options.A: Descriptive analytics establishes trusted definitions and baselines needed to validate any prediction
options.B: Predictions are not allowed in business intelligence
options.C: Descriptive analytics is cheaper and therefore always done first

questions.explanation: A forecast is only as credible as the history and definitions behind it. Descriptive work provides those baselines and the reference for checking predictions.
